subject: Next steps: demo + dedicated GPU pool sizing

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@evopay.com>, Evan Chung <evan.chung@evopay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: demo + dedicated GPU pool sizing

Hi Priya & Evan,

Thanks again for a productive discovery earlier — really appreciated the clarity on Evopay's fraud-detection and ticketing use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goals: integrate Redwood for real-time scoring and async batch reranks; primary SLO is p95 latency <= 150ms for online scoring, while batch reranks can tolerate higher latency.
- Current workload estimate (from call): ~250 QPS sustained with short bursts to ~600 QPS during peak events; average prompt length ~220 tokens, peak sequence length ~1024 tokens.
- Models: you mentioned wanting a 70B-quality open model (quantized) for production; we'll confirm exact model variant on the sizing call.

Request: let's lock a 60–75 minute technical deep-dive / sizing session to: 1) validate traffic shape and sequence lengths, 2) review KV-cache and batching tradeoffs, and 3) produce a first-pass dedicated GPU pool recommendation.

Proposed slots (PT):
- Mon Apr 18 — 10:00–11:15 AM PT
- Mon Apr 18 — 1:00–2:15 PM PT
- Tue Apr 19 — 9:00–10:15 AM PT

If none of those work, send two alternatives and we'll accommodate. Also: could you share a small workload sample (CSV with timestamps, prompt length, and qps-by-window) ahead of the call? I can run it through our quick estimator and bring preliminary numbers.

For prep, I've attached our 1-page sizing checklist and a link to the initial HubSpot record for the deal.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Alex — thanks for the summary and the checklist, that helps. Confirming the numbers on the call are a good approximation of where we sit today (250 QPS average, burst to ~600). We do have a mix of short scoring requests (~50–150 tokens) and longer contextual requests up to ~1k tokens when we attach recent history.

I've attached a small sample of our event stream and a CSV with per-minute QPS from a recent peak window — should be enough for a first pass. We prefer US data residency.

For the deep-dive, Mon Apr 18 at 10:00 AM PT works for Evan and me. If you or Ben need to shift, please let us know.

Thanks — locking the Mon Apr 18 10:00 AM PT slot on my calendar. I'll be the primary on the sizing side. A few quick asks so I can prep:

- Can you confirm the 95th percentile prompt+response length and the distribution of short vs long requests? If you don't have exact percentiles, approximate bins are fine.
- Do you expect KV cache reuse across requests (i.e., repeated context across many users)? That affects memory footprint.
- Any hard constraints on preemptible GPUs or must be dedicated/guaranteed instances?

I'll prepare an initial workbook and attach a first-pass capacity spreadsheet to the invite. That will include: recommended GPU types, pool sizes, expected sustained token throughput, and a staging plan for canary rollout.

Alex — if we want to include a short (10–15 min) product demo at the top of the call, say 10:00–10:15, I can run the sizing portion starting at ~10:20.

Ben Carter
